trial_court: Additional District Judge (ADJ) Delhi, HMA No. 58 of 583 of 2003
case_name: Shobha Gupta vs Rajesh Gupta And Anr.
facts_of_case: Appellant Shobha Gupta filed for divorce against respondent Rajesh Gupta on grounds of adultery, cruelty, and desertion. Appellant claimed she was earlier married to Kailash Jain and had a daughter and son from that marriage. Trial court dismissed the petition as appellant failed to produce proof of her earlier marriage being dissolved.

legal_principles.principle: The burden of proof lies on the person who contests a valid marriage.
legal_principles.held: It is fairly well settled now in a series of decisions that the burden of proof lies on the person who contests a valid marriage.
cited_cases: Neelavva v. The Divisional Collector, K.S.R.T.C.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the person who contests a valid marriage to satisfy the court that the first marriage stood dissolved.
legal_principles.held: In this case, in the first place it was the trial court itself which required the appellant (i.e. the petitioner before it), to satisfy the court that the first marriage with Shri Kailash Jain stood dissolved by a decree of divorce by mutual consent.
cited_cases: Neelavva v. The Divisional Collector, K.S.R.T.C.

outcome.final_order: Trial court's judgment was upheld, dismissing the divorce petition.
